title: Observable's design flaw, and Observer against Pub/Sub

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: `StockTicker extends Model` needs to notify observers. Per the page, what is the problem with using `java.util.Observable`?

options.text: Observable is declared final, so no class such as StockTicker may extend it.
options.says: Observable was built to be subclassed; the page's complaint is that subclassing is the only way to use it.

options.text: Observable is a class, so a subclass such as StockTicker gives up its one superclass.
options.says: Java has single inheritance of classes, so a class that extends Model cannot also extend Observable; that is the first flaw the page lists.

options.text: Observable is an interface, so a class such as StockTicker must write every method.
options.says: The trouble is the reverse: Observable is a class, and an interface is exactly what the page recommends instead.

questions.stem: What separates Publish/Subscribe from the Observer pattern, in the page's comparison?

options.text: Publishers and subscribers hold no reference to each other; a broker routes each message.
options.says: In Pub/Sub publishers send to a topic and the broker delivers, so neither side knows the other, unlike an Observer subject.

options.text: Publishers hold each subscriber and call it directly through that reference.
options.says: That describes Observer itself: the subject keeps references to its observers and calls them.

options.text: One mediator object holds the rules for how publishers and subscribers interact.
options.says: That describes Mediator, where components talk through a coordinator that encapsulates their interaction.

concepts: java.util.Observable was deprecated in Java 9 because it is a class rather than an interface, is not type-safe and leaves order and threading unspecified.
Observer links a subject directly to its observers, Pub/Sub puts a broker between publishers and subscribers, and Mediator centralises interaction logic.
